title: *CS521 & CS511 – GDB SOLUTION*
text:
*CS521 & CS511 – GDB SOLUTION*

*My Choice:* Approach A Organizing Website Content Using HTML Tables and Forms

I would choose *Approach A* because an online event management website needs to present structured event information clearly and provide a simple way for visitors to register online.

 *1. Proper HTML Structure:* HTML tables use appropriate elements such as `<table>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>` to organize event names, dates, venues, speakers, and registration fees. This makes information structured and easier to understand.

*2. Easy Comparison and Readability:* Tables allow visitors to compare event schedules and registration fees conveniently. CSS properties such as borders, spacing, text alignment, and background colours can further improve readability.

*3. Simple and Accessible Registration:* HTML forms provide suitable controls such as text fields, email inputs, dropdown menus, radio buttons, and checkboxes. These make it easier for visitors to enter their details and register for events.

*4. Better Navigation:* HTML links and lists help visitors move easily between event categories, schedules, and registration pages, improving the overall user experience.

*5. Maintainability and Web Standards:* Approach A follows fundamental HTML principles by using semantic elements for their intended purposes. It keeps content well-organized and allows CSS styling to be managed separately, making the website easier to maintain and update.

*So in my Opinion* Approach A is the better choice because it directly addresses the website's main requirements: displaying structured event information, comparing registration fees, providing accessible registration forms, and ensuring easy navigation. CSS Flexbox and positioning can also be incorporated later to enhance the website's visual layout.

> 𝑽𝒊𝒓𝒕𝒖𝒂𝒍 𝑼𝒏𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒔𝒊𝒕𝒚 | 𝑺𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝑯𝒖𝒃 🦋🎓📚

title: *CS521 GDB Solution*
text:
*CS521 GDB Solution*

Selected Approach: Approach A – Organizing Website Content Using HTML Tables and Forms


I would choose Approach A for developing the online event management website for the following reasons:


Structured Information: HTML tables provide an organized way to display event names, dates, venues, speakers, schedules, and registration fees, making information easy to compare.
User-Friendly Registration: HTML forms allow visitors to submit their personal details, select events, and choose registration options conveniently through input fields, dropdown menus, and checkboxes.
Accessibility and Readability: Semantic HTML elements such as table headings, labels, and lists improve content understanding and make the website easier to navigate.
Easy Navigation: HTML links and lists help users move between different event categories, schedules, and registration pages without confusion.
Maintainability: Using appropriate HTML elements makes the website structure clear, organized, and easier to update in the future.

Conclusion: Approach A is more appropriate because the main purpose of this website is to present structured event information and provide a reliable online registration facility.
